title: Compare contrasting short sources and evaluate evidence

questions.prompt: Two articles use different sample sizes. What must a fair comparison note?
choices: The populations and sampling methods differ.
The larger article title proves stronger findings.
Both samples automatically describe every citizen.
questions.explanation: Sample design affects what conclusions can be compared.

questions.prompt: Which formulation attributes a claim to a specific source?
choices: Il est évident que tout le monde a gagné.
Les effets sont connus sans enquête.
Selon le rapport municipal, l'accès a progressé.
questions.explanation: Selon le rapport municipal makes source attribution explicit.

questions.prompt: Choose a cautious contrast between two reports.
choices: Tout désaccord prouve que les deux sont faux.
L'un constate une hausse; l'autre ne la retrouve pas.
Les deux rapports sont identiques par définition.
questions.explanation: The wording distinguishes the findings without inventing a cause.

questions.prompt: Which connector introduces a counterpoint?
choices: En revanche,
Par conséquent,
Notamment,
questions.explanation: En revanche contrasts one source's conclusion with another.

questions.prompt: Which question examines methodological differences?
choices: Quel rapport a le papier le plus brillant ?
Quel auteur écrit le plus de pages ?
Les deux études utilisent-elles les mêmes définitions ?
questions.explanation: Comparable definitions matter when interpreting conflicting findings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence appropriately limits a finding?
choices: La hausse restera identique pour toujours.
Dans les trois quartiers étudiés, la fréquentation a augmenté.
La fréquentation a augmenté dans tous les pays.
questions.explanation: The first statement limits its scope to the three studied neighborhoods.

questions.prompt: Choose a reasoned response to incompatible measurements.
choices: Comparer les dates et les indicateurs retenus.
Choisir automatiquement les chiffres les plus élevés.
Supprimer le rapport le plus ancien sans examen.
questions.explanation: Different time windows and indicators may explain discrepancies.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces a source limitation?
choices: Par conséquent, les résultats sont infaillibles.
En effet, toute critique est impossible.
Toutefois, l'échantillon est restreint.
questions.explanation: Toutefois flags a limitation that qualifies the evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the balanced conclusion.
choices: Une seule source suffit à tout prouver.
Les données suggèrent une tendance, à vérifier ailleurs.
La tendance vaut sans exception pour tous.
questions.explanation: A cautious conclusion acknowledges uncertainty and generalizability limits.

questions.prompt: Source A: « 60 % des 50 répondants utilisent le service ». How many respondents is that?
choices: Thirty respondents.
Sixty respondents.
Fifty-five respondents.
questions.explanation: Sixty percent of fifty equals thirty.

questions.prompt: Source B: « 60 % des 500 répondants utilisent le service ». What changes versus A?
choices: The percentage becomes one hundred percent.
The finding is automatically true for everyone.
The sample count is larger, though representativeness still requires review.
questions.explanation: The same percentage with more respondents does not by itself prove representativeness.

questions.prompt: Source A concerns 2021; B concerns 2025. What must be considered?
choices: The earlier report has no usable information.
The observations refer to different years.
The reports must refer to the same period.
questions.explanation: Temporal change may explain differences between findings.

questions.prompt: A text says « l'association affirme » while another says « les données montrent ». What differs?
choices: One attributes a claim, the other presents a data-based interpretation.
Both always identify direct experimental proof.
Neither expression provides any information.
questions.explanation: Reporting verbs convey different kinds of claims and warrants.

questions.prompt: One source surveys students and another surveys parents. What is a key difference?
choices: The school cannot have families.
The two groups must give identical answers.
The populations being asked are not identical.
questions.explanation: Distinct respondent groups may have different views and experiences.

questions.prompt: An infographic omits the denominator for percentages. What cannot be checked?
choices: Whether any color appears.
What total population each percentage represents.
Whether the infographic uses text.
questions.explanation: Percentages need a denominator for reliable interpretation.

questions.prompt: A newspaper column defends a policy; a statistical report measures participation. What differs?
choices: The text genres and purposes.
Both texts are automatically surveys.
The opinion column is necessarily a law.
questions.explanation: A column argues; a report may describe measured outcomes.

questions.prompt: A report describes correlation but its headline says « causes ». What concern arises?
choices: The headline is automatically confirmed.
Correlation proves every cause.
The headline overstates causal evidence.
questions.explanation: Observational association alone does not establish causation.

questions.prompt: Two sources disagree on costs, but one includes maintenance. What explains the gap?
choices: Neither report can discuss money.
They calculate different cost categories.
Maintenance is always free.
questions.explanation: Comparisons must account for included and excluded expenses.

questions.prompt: You compare two reports in class. Which opening avoids false equivalence?
choices: Les études examinent des contextes différents et ne répondent pas exactement à la même question.
Les études ont des titres différents donc l'une ment.
Toute divergence disparaît si l'on arrondit les chiffres.
questions.explanation: Their distinct questions and contexts should be stated before comparing.

questions.prompt: One author cites an interview; the other cites administrative records. What should you do?
choices: Declare interviews universally invalid.
Assume administrative records capture every experience.
Explain how the evidence types support different claims.
questions.explanation: Evidence types answer different questions and have different limitations.

questions.prompt: You want to make a comparison table. Which headings are most useful?
choices: Author's age and length of title only.
Source, date, sample, measure, conclusion and limitation.
Cover color, page count and favorite font only.
questions.explanation: A sound comparison tracks methodology, findings and limits.

questions.prompt: You notice that a study uses an outdated definition. How should you proceed?
choices: Clarify the definition before comparing its figures.
Copy the numbers without a caveat.
Conclude the study must be fabricated.
questions.explanation: Definition shifts can undermine direct comparability.

questions.prompt: Which sentence fairly acknowledges a counterclaim?
choices: Le second rapport est absurde parce qu'il diverge.
Une étude contraire doit être supprimée.
Le second rapport observe un effet différent, mais sa période est plus courte.
questions.explanation: The shorter observation window is a relevant limitation, not a reason for dismissal.

questions.prompt: A press release quotes only the best-performing group. What should you seek?
choices: No further information, because the quote is positive.
The results for all measured groups and any selection criteria.
Only the photograph accompanying the release.
questions.explanation: Selective reporting can misrepresent the full dataset.

questions.prompt: Two authors interpret the same numbers differently. What is the next step?
choices: Identify their assumptions and inferential steps.
Assume both interpretations are proven.
Choose the writer with the stronger adjectives.
questions.explanation: Interpretations can diverge through different assumptions.

questions.prompt: A student claims a nationwide effect based on one city. Which revision is fair?
choices: Dans toutes les villes, le même effet est certain.
Cette étude prouve le résultat pour chaque pays.
Dans cette ville, les résultats indiquent un effet possible.
questions.explanation: A one-city study cannot establish universal nationwide effects.

questions.prompt: You need a synthesis rather than a summary of one source. Which is best?
choices: Je préfère le style du deuxième auteur.
Les deux sources constatent une hausse, mais divergent sur ses causes possibles.
La première source a cinq pages.
questions.explanation: Synthesis connects agreement and disagreement across sources.
